questions.prompt: In the sample library XML, every `<book>` sits inside a `<section>`. Which expression returns all three `<book>` elements?
questions.explanation: `//` is descendant-or-self, so `//book` finds book nodes anywhere below, no matter how deeply they are nested. `/` only steps to direct children.

questions.prompt: `doc` holds the lesson's sample library XML (titles: *Mastering C#*, *XML Basics*, *Space Odyssey*). What does this print?
questions.explanation: `contains(title,'XML')` keeps only books whose title contains "XML", which is book B2, so its title `XML Basics` is printed.

questions.prompt: What does `//section/@name` return for the sample XML?
options: The two `<section>` elements with all their books
questions.explanation: `@` selects attributes, so the expression returns the `name` attribute of each `<section>`: `Programming` and `Fiction`.

questions.prompt: The books cost 49.99 (B1), 29.50 (B2) and 19.99 (B3). What does `//book[price > 30]` return?
options: All three books, with prices compared as text
questions.explanation: A predicate `[...]` filters the selected nodes; only B1 has a price greater than 30, and the expression returns the `<book>` itself, not its price.

questions.prompt: You have already selected a `<title>` node. What does `../@id` return?
questions.explanation: `..` moves to the parent node, so `../@id` reads the parent book's `id` attribute; `.` would stay on the current node.
